summary: Run 8 of M1-S03 — the fifth § 4 test-only repair, after reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 11 (S2-F-16). Run 11 showed 35/35 tests passing and 86.2% aggregate coverage, yet still failed validation on a per-class floor: Tier2EscalationService individually at 53.659%, under the 75% RunSpecifiedTests enforces per class. reports/mock-deploy/2026-09-12T17-17-07Z/result.json's codeCoverage array (recorded at run 9) named the 19 uncovered lines out of 41; read against the class body they resolve to exactly two branches — the empty/null-input early return (line 44) and the EventBus.publish() rejection path (building an Integration_Failure__c row, the conditional insert, and the whole errorText() helper: lines 84-96, 106, 119-127) — neither reachable from the trigger-driven path every existing test in Tier2EscalationServiceTest uses. Added two methods that call Tier2EscalationService.escalate(List<Case>) directly: escalateWithNoCasesReturnsImmediately (line 44) and escalateWithAMissingCaseNumberWritesAPublishFailureRowAndStillEnqueuesTheJob, which forces a deterministic publish rejection via Tier2_Escalation__e.Case_Number__c's required=true constraint (M1-S01) rather than the FLS-based mechanism S2-F-13 used, since this build's current permission sets bundle both grants together and can no longer construct that asymmetry. Both new methods register a 2xx MockHttpResponseGenerator before calling escalate(), applying § 0e's lesson (S2-F-15) proactively, since escalate() unconditionally enqueues a Tier2WebhookQueueable regardless of publish outcome. No shipped class, no other test method, and no other file changed.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM. Gate B: 0 unresolved symbols — both new methods call only Tier2EscalationService's own public/@TestVisible members (escalate, STATUS_NEW, SEVERITY_ERROR) and the required=true constraint on Tier2_Escalation__e.Case_Number__c is read directly from artefacts/M1-S01's own object metadata, not recalled. Gate C check 3 (compile) did not run in this agent — design-only, no target_org_alias — but this run applies a now twice-confirmed-by-the-org lesson (§ 0e/S2-F-15: an enqueued job runs to completion regardless of Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() wrapping) proactively rather than reactively, which is why this is not capped lower. What keeps this at MEDIUM rather than HIGH: no agent in this loop can confirm Tier2EscalationService's coverage actually clears 75% after this run, or that EventBus.publish() truly returns a rejected (not thrown) SaveResult for a required-field violation the same way it does for the FLS violation S2-F-13 already confirmed — that specific claim is inferred from the class's own header comment and Q11's answer (EventBus.publish never throws), not independently re-verified against an org for this exact failure mode.

findings.title: The publish-rejection test uses a different trigger mechanism than S2-F-13's, because the current permission sets can no longer reproduce that one
findings.detail: S2-F-13's rejection (mock-deploy run 8) came from a user lacking Tier2_Escalation__e Create while still holding Integration_Failure__c Create — an asymmetry that existed only because the two grants were added to Tier2_Webhook_Admin at different times. Now that both live in the same permission set (the S2-F-13 fix), no shipped permission set can reproduce that specific asymmetry without a bespoke, test-local PermissionSet built via DML — not attempted here. This run instead uses Tier2_Escalation__e.Case_Number__c's required=true constraint, a different and arguably more robust trigger for the same sr.isSuccess()==false branch, since it needs no second user or permission grant at all.
findings.recommendation: None needed for this step — recorded so a future reader does not wonder why this test doesn't mirror S2-F-13's exact mechanism.

findings.title: Per-class coverage floors were invisible to every prior run of this step until this one
findings.detail: reports/mock-deploy/2026-09-12T17-17-07Z/result.json (run 9) already recorded Tier2EscalationService's 19-of-41 uncovered lines, but every finding on this step through S2-F-14 (run 9) and S2-F-15 (run 10) was read off the aggregate coverage_pct, which stayed at or above the aggregate floor's failure threshold for a different reason each time. The per-class enforcement only became visible once the aggregate genuinely cleared 75% (run 11) and the platform's per-class floor was the only thing left to fail on.
findings.recommendation: A future dry-run summary tool item: print the full codeCoverageWarnings array (per-class floor violations) alongside the aggregate number on every run, not only when the aggregate itself fails — mirrors the tool item already named for coverage-under-75% in run 9's own note.

process_observations.observation: S2-F-15's lesson (an enqueued job runs to completion regardless of Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() wrapping) was applied proactively here — both new methods register a mock before calling escalate() without needing a second failing dry run to discover the necessity first.

The exact uncovered-line list was already on file (result.json's codeCoverage array from run 9) rather than needing to be re-derived or guessed — reading it against the class body directly produced a precise map from line numbers to branches, with no ambiguity about what to test.

This is the third distinct coverage/test-only finding on this one step in a row (S2-F-14, S2-F-15, S2-F-16), each surfaced only after the previous one was fixed and a fresh dry run ran. The pattern suggests dry runs against this step have been finding issues serially rather than exhaustively — each run reveals the next problem the previous one was masking (aggregate coverage masked the per-class floor; the per-class floor was itself invisible until aggregate cleared).

Whether EventBus.publish() treats a required-field violation on a platform event exactly like the FLS violation S2-F-13 already confirmed — returning a rejected SaveResult rather than throwing — is inferred from Tier2EscalationService's own header comment and Q11's answer, not independently confirmed by this run against an org for this specific failure mode.
A fresh dry run with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests is the only way to confirm Tier2EscalationService now individually clears 75% and that 37/37 tests pass.
